title: School Notebooks 5-pack

drivers.name: Price increase (2.3%)
drivers.evidence: Two recent weeks at $9.03 saw 10 and 7 units (x1.32 and x0.92 vs baseline). Average x1.12, but 2026-10-05 (no event) was below baseline. Noise-adjusted effect of past promotions is weak (x1.16). Price increase likely suppresses demand; shrink toward 1.0.

drivers.name: Heatwave (38°C)
drivers.evidence: No historical evidence linking extreme heat to notebook demand. But high temperatures may reduce store traffic. Conservative downside adjustment based on plausible behavioral impact.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 7.6. No events or promotions are scheduled. The price is 2.3% above regular, which historically correlates with a 15% lift in units (2026-09-28: $9.03 → 10 units, vs baseline 7.6 → x1.32). The 2026-10-05 week (same price, no event) sold 7 units (x0.92). Heatwave (38°C) may reduce foot traffic, but no evidence links heat to demand drops for notebooks. The noise-adjusted lift from past promotions is weak (x1.16), and no post-promo dip observed. The classical model's x1.00 is appropriate. Price increase likely suppresses demand slightly. No strong signal to override baseline. Adjust marginally down for price and uncertainty.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 7.6 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 35.7 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 23.2

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-64% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
